ai.thread_title: Inkling 2 Small: 17A-594B trained in 68 hours, beats Muse Spark
ai.name: Latent Space / AINews
ai.hook: Inkling 2 Small trained in 68 hours on 12T tokens, outperforms Muse Spark.
insights: **17A-594B parameter model** completed training in 68 hours using 12 trillion tokens
Performance beats **Muse Spark** on multiple benchmarks despite training speed
Signals aggressive efficiency in frontier model training pipelines
ai.for_you: If you're shipping agents to Portuguese SMBs, faster training cycles mean faster model iteration and cheaper fine-tuning for domain-specific tasks. Watch this as a signal of cost pressure on inference and training economics.
ai.context: Inkling is a new model family from an emerging lab. The speed-to-performance ratio is notable because it suggests training efficiency improvements are real, not just hype. This changes cost assumptions for building production agent systems.
ai.what_changed: Confirmed release with concrete training metrics and benchmark comparisons.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only hard evidence of a major model release this week with concrete training data.

ai.thread_title: LLMs can read and write neural network weights directly as text
ai.name: Rikiya Takehi et al. / Latent Space
ai.hook: Frontier models interpret raw model weights as text, modify reasoning loops without retraining.
insights: **GPT-6 Astra and Qwen 3.8 27B** both demonstrated ability to read, interpret, and edit neural network weights as floating-point text
Enables direct **reasoning loop modification** without full fine-tuning or inference-time scaling
Cuts **AutoResearch out of the RSI loop**: agents can now debug and optimize their own reasoning directly
ai.for_you: This is a practical breakthrough for agency work. You could prompt an agent to inspect its own weight distributions, identify bottlenecks in reasoning, and push edits—all within a conversation. For Portuguese SMBs running custom workflows, this means iterative model customization without data science overhead.
ai.context: Weight-Space Programming is a formal technique discovered this week. Frontier models can now treat neural network parameters as interpretable, editable data structures. This moves from 'models are black boxes' to 'models can be debugged and tuned conversationally.'
ai.what_changed: Qwen 3.8 27B (open-weight) demonstrated the capability independently, confirming it's not a frontier-only artifact. This expands deployment options.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: First credible evidence that model internals can be treated as conversational objects; changes agent design fundamentally.

ai.thread_title: Realtime-Bench: frontier models fail on sub-500ms decision tasks
ai.name: Import AI / Jack Clark
ai.hook: Frontier models cannot reliably decide or act faster than 500ms; real-time tasks remain unsolved.
insights: **Realtime-Bench benchmark** tests decision latency on auction, gaming, and real-time trading tasks
Even GPT-6 Astra fails consistently on tasks requiring sub-500ms responses
Highlights structural gap between reasoning depth and execution speed
ai.for_you: For agency work with Portuguese SMBs, this means real-time applications (trading, live customer service, bidding systems) still require deterministic code, not agentic LLMs. Agent value sits in medium-horizon tasks (hour to day scale), not sub-second decisions.
ai.what_changed: Benchmark now published with detailed breakdowns; confirms earlier signals that latency is hard constraint, not engineering problem.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Cuts through hype about agents replacing everything; concrete decision boundary for what agents can and cannot do.
